record.context_brief: Scars in Katok's Finsler metric example
record.original_question: In Katok's example of a Finsler metric on the two-dimensional sphere with ergodic geodesic flow and only two periodic orbits, do the closed geodesics correspond to scars?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 48 (A. Katok) . Do the closed geodesics in this example correspond to scars?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Katok constructed a smooth Finsler (non-reversible) metric on the two-dimensional sphere $S^2$ whose geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle is ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure and possesses exactly two closed (prime) geodesics. Consider the quantization of this geodesic flow (for example, via a sequence of semiclassical operators or Laplace-type operators whose principal symbol generates the flow), and the associated sequence of normalized eigenfunctions $\{\psi_n\}$ with eigenvalues tending to infinity. A "scar" is said to occur along a closed orbit $\gamma$ if some subsequence of the microlocal lifts (Wigner measures) of $\{\psi_n\}$ has a weak-* limit that is not the Liouville measure and assigns positive mass to $\gamma$ (equivalently, the eigenfunctions concentrate, in phase space, on $\gamma$ along the subsequence).

Question: In Katok's Finsler 2-sphere example, do the two closed geodesics correspond to scars, i.e., is there a sequence of eigenfunctions whose microlocal limits charge these closed orbits, despite the classical ergodicity of the geodesic flow?
artifact.category_tag: Quantum scars and ergodic geodesic flows
artifact.status_search_result: A web search yields work on Katok's Finsler 2-sphere example, on its ergodicity, and on the existence of exactly two closed geodesics (Bangert–Long), as well as general quantum ergodicity results, but no source directly establishes or refutes the existence of quantum scars on the two closed geodesics in this particular example. The status appears to be unresolved in the accessible literature.

status_evidence.title: The existence of two closed geodesics on every Finsler 2-sphere
status_evidence.snippet: Bangert and Long: every Finsler metric on S^2 carries at least two closed geodesics, showing Katok's example is optimal.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the classical (non-quantum) optimality of Katok's example; does not address scars.

status_evidence.title: Reeb dynamics inspired by Katok's example in Finsler geometry
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work explores Reeb-dynamical analogues of Katok's example.
status_evidence.claim: Recent investigations of Katok's example focus on classical dynamics, not on quantum scarring.

status_evidence.title: Ergodic components and topological entropy in geodesic flows of surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies ergodicity of geodesic flows on surfaces following Katok's construction.
status_evidence.claim: Concerns classical ergodic properties; no scar analysis.
